answers.answer: Each player starts with 25 money; 1 worker active and 3 inactive; draw 8 Zoo cards and keep 4; draw 2 Final Scoring cards. Put Action cards side I up, Animals in slot 1 (leftmost, strength 1), and randomly place the other four in the remaining slots. Appeal starts at 0 for the first player, 1 for second, 2 for third, and 3 for fourth.
answers.evidence: Personal setup D: ‘Take 25 money’; C3: ‘1 association worker ... active’ and ‘remaining 3’; E: ‘Draw 2 Final Scoring cards’; F: ‘Draw 8 Zoo cards; keep 4’; B: ‘side I up’ and Animals under the leftmost slot. C1 lists appeal spaces 0, 1, 2, 3 by turn order.

answers.answer: For 4 players, place 4 face-up Base Conservation Project cards; otherwise place 3. In a 2-player game, block one reward level on each of the three face-up base projects (left level on left card, middle on middle card, right on right card) and block the three spaces in the donation area's left column; these are unavailable to both players. Three-player games have 3 face-up base projects and no stated blocks; four-player games have 4 and no stated blocks. Reveal the initial six-card display after all players have chosen their hand cards.
answers.evidence: Setup 5b specifies four face-up in a 4-player game and otherwise three. Setup 5c specifies the blocked project levels and donation spaces for 2 players. Personal setup G says reveal the 6 cards after everyone chooses hand cards.

answers.answer: After using the card in slot 4, remove it, shift cards from slots 1–3 one slot right, then place the used card in slot 1. Set strength before the action; each X-token spent adds +1 strength, and X-tokens gained during that action cannot boost it. You may spend any number, but may hold at most 5 X-tokens. Complete an action, including moving the Action cards, before resolving an effect that says ‘after finishing.’
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: remove the card, shift cards left of the empty slot right, and place used card in slot 1. X-tokens: set strength before acting; each adds +1; maximum 5; gained tokens cannot boost that action. ‘After finishing’ effects follow completion and card movement.

answers.answer: No: you may not do nothing, including playing zero animals or building zero buildings. Instead, take exactly 1 X-token: select an Action card, move it to slot 1, and shift intervening cards right. Its strength and upgrade state do not matter. You cannot use this action while holding 5 X-tokens.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure says ‘You may not do nothing.’ X-token action: select a card, move it to slot 1 and shift intervening cards; strength and upgrade state are irrelevant; unavailable at 5 held tokens.

answers.answer: When the Break token reaches the last space, any extra steps beyond it are ignored, and the player who reached it gains 1 X-token. The break occurs after the triggering player's current turn ends; finish the turn. After the break, the token returns to its starting space and play continues clockwise with the next player. A normal break does not itself give extra turns.
answers.evidence: Break track: ‘break takes place after the end of your current turn,’ gain 1 X-token, and ‘Ignore any additional steps beyond the last space.’ Break procedure resets the token; Player Reference says play continues and a normal break alone grants no extra turns.

answers.answer: Both sides advance the Break token 2 spaces. Side I then either draws from the deck according to its table (up to 3 cards, with a possible discard) or snaps exactly 1 display card of any reputation at strength 5+; snapping replaces drawing. Side II may draw from the deck and/or from within reputation range in any order using the upgraded table, or snap exactly 1 display card of any reputation at strength 3+ (strength above 3 adds nothing to a snap); reputation range restricts only the Side-II draw option. Cards taken from the display are not replenished until the turn is complete. Hand limit is checked at breaks only, not during the turn.
answers.evidence: Cards action: each side advances Break 2; Side I draw or strength-5 snap; Side II deck and/or reputation-range draws or strength-3 snap. ‘On either side, snapping takes exactly one display card of any reputation, with no deck draw.’ Replenish at turn end; discard to hand limit during breaks.

answers.answer: Reputation range includes the display card in the folder matching your Reputation counter and every lower-numbered folder. Reputation 10+ requires the upgraded Cards action. At reputation 15, additional reputation does not move the counter; gain 1 appeal for each remaining reputation step instead. You may not look through the discard pile during the game.
answers.evidence: ‘Within reputation range’ is the matching folder plus all lower-numbered folders; 10+ requires upgraded Cards; at 15 further reputation gives 1 appeal per step; ‘You may not look through the discard pile.’

answers.answer: Build I builds exactly 1 building with size no greater than action strength; Build II builds any number of different buildings whose total size is at most strength, with no duplicate building in the same action. Pay 2 money per space before placing each building. The first building must have at least one space on a map border; later buildings must touch an existing building by at least one edge. Build only on empty spaces, without extending off-map, overlapping, or covering water/rock. Restricted-icon spaces require Build II. Kiosks must be at least 3 spaces apart (at least 2 spaces between kiosks). Each pavilion immediately and only once gives 1 appeal.
answers.evidence: Build I/II limits and cost are specified under BUILD. Placement rules give first/later placement, prohibited spaces and Build II restriction; kiosk spacing is ‘at least 3 spaces’; ‘Each pavilion ... increases ... appeal by 1.’

answers.answer: Build I offers kiosks, pavilions, standard enclosures sizes 1–5, and a size-3 Petting Zoo. Build II also makes the size-5 Reptile House and Large Bird Aviary available. Components list 4 of each special enclosure type: 4 Petting Zoos, 4 Reptile Houses, and 4 Large Bird Aviaries. Build cannot create unique buildings; those enter only through Sponsor cards. Covering every map space except water and rock immediately grants 7 appeal.
answers.evidence: BUILD lists available buildings by side, size and one-per-zoo special enclosure limits; Components gives 4 of each special enclosure. BUILD II states unique buildings only enter via Sponsor cards and full map coverage grants 7 appeal.

answers.answer: Yes. Bonuses gained earlier in an action, including money, cards, and newly activated workers, may be used in later steps; resolve items one at a time, and pay each item before receiving its own benefits. For an animal, for example, pay its full cost before money-gain effects from playing it pay out. Immediate effects resolve at their stated point; ‘after finishing’ effects wait until the whole action is complete and the Action card has moved. For multiple simultaneous effects, the owning player chooses their order. Association II also resolves tasks in sequence, so workers or bonuses gained earlier in that action may be used for later tasks.
answers.evidence: X-tokens section: earlier action bonuses may be used later; ‘You must pay each item before receiving its own benefits.’ Animal action says pay cost before later effects and distinguishes immediate from after-finishing effects. Association II resolves tasks in sequence; simultaneous effects are ordered by the owning player.

answers.answer: To play an animal, meet all its left-side conditions, pay its cost, house it legally, place its card, and resolve its effects. A partner zoo on the animal's continent reduces cost by 3 money per continent icon on the card, so a double icon reduces it by 6. An animal other than a Petting Zoo animal may use an empty standard enclosure at least its required size; flip the whole enclosure to its occupied side. Some require adjacency to one or two water and/or rock spaces; count distinct adjacent hexes. Petting Zoo animals go only in the Petting Zoo. Reptiles and some birds may use a Reptile House or Large Bird Aviary if shown as suitable; put supply player tokens on the indicated number of spaces, and never flip special enclosures. Effects such as appeal resolve after housing and playing the card; ordinary effects are immediate (including before a second animal), while after-finishing effects wait until the Animals action and card movement are complete. Simultaneous effects may be ordered by the player.
answers.evidence: Animals action gives conditions, payment and the 3-money reduction ‘per continent icon,’ enclosure and distinct terrain adjacency rules, token marking for special enclosures, and effect timing.

answers.answer: Animals II permits animals from the display within reputation range as well as from hand; pay an additional amount equal to the display folder number. The two animals, if playing two, may be any mix of hand and display, and display cards are replenished only at turn end. At strength 5+, you may first gain 1 reputation at the very beginning of the action, raising your range before selecting display animals. Side II also permits animals whose conditions show the upgrade-required icon.
answers.evidence: Animals Side II: display cards within reputation range, additional folder-number cost, mix hand/display, no refill until turn ends; at strength 5+ gain reputation at the very beginning; permits upgrade-icon conditions.

answers.answer: Only when building a Reptile House or Large Bird Aviary, immediately, and only once per building, may you move suitable animals from standard enclosures into it. Suitable animals are reptiles or birds shown as eligible for that special enclosure. The summary gives no fixed count of animals: each moved animal uses the number of special spaces indicated on its card, marked with supply player tokens, and moves only if enough free spaces remain. For each moved animal, flip the smallest occupied standard enclosure meeting all its requirements (including water/rock) to empty. If none meets all requirements, use the smallest occupied enclosure meeting its size requirement; if none meets even the size, flip none. Decide separately for each animal.
answers.evidence: Build II allows moving suitable animals ‘immediately — and only once per building.’ Special-enclosure capacity is marked with the number of spaces on the card. Special Rules give the smallest-enclosure selection and size-only fallback, or none if no enclosure meets size; decide per animal.

answers.answer: Association task strengths are: increase reputation 2, gain partner zoo 3, gain university 4, and conservation project work 5. Side I performs exactly one task. Side II performs one or more different tasks whose total task value is no greater than action strength. Each task needs a worker; if one of your workers is already on that task, place 2 workers to repeat it; if 3 of your workers are there, you cannot do it again before the break. Other players' workers do not matter. Side II allows 1 or 2 of your workers per task as above.
answers.evidence: Association I lists each task and strength, with repeat-task worker requirements and says other players' workers do not matter. Association II allows one or more different tasks, total value at most strength, and ‘1 or 2 of your workers per task.’

answers.answer: Partner zoos and universities are taken from available tiles on the Association board and placed bottom-up in their respective columns on your zoo map; take any printed placement bonus immediately, and take a university's reputation bonus if shown. The FAQ confirms a bonus granting one takes an available board tile, not one from general supply. You cannot take a duplicate university; partner zoos must be from different continents and are limited to 4, with the third or fourth requiring Association II. Universities are the only way to raise hand limit to 5; otherwise it is 3, enforced at breaks. After a break, replenish zoos and universities to make each available exactly once, skipping any that all players already have.
answers.evidence: Association tasks specify taking zoo/university tiles from the board, placement bonuses, no duplicate university, distinct continents and partner limit. FAQ specifies board tile source. Break procedure replenishes them; hand limit is 3 or 5 with a particular university.

answers.answer: Conservation work may support a project already in play, or play a project card from hand and support it immediately; Association II can also play a new project from the in-range display for the folder-number cost. A new card enters the leftmost space above the Association board and pushes existing cards right; the row holds up to 2, 3, or 4 cards depending on player count. Support an unoccupied condition whose requirements you meet, using one player token of your choice from the 7 tokens at the left edge of your zoo map. You may support a given project only once. Removing the token activates its map bonus immediately; choose whether to take it before or after the project reward. If the row limit is exceeded, discard the rightmost project and return its tokens to their owners' supplies (the already activated map bonuses stay active).
answers.evidence: Association project-work rules state how new projects enter, row limits, support conditions/token source/once limit, and immediate bonus timing. Side II adds display projects with folder cost. Special Rules say discarded project tokens return to supply, while bonuses stay activated.

answers.answer: Yes. A release project requires the animal's printed standard-enclosure size to match the depicted size exactly, even if it could also live in a special enclosure. Discarding it loses only its printed appeal before conservation is gained; discard the card and lose its icons. Keep conservation, reputation, ability-generated appeal, and earlier effects already earned. To free space, if the animal could live in a special enclosure, first remove its indicated special-enclosure tokens if possible; otherwise flip the smallest occupied standard enclosure meeting all the animal's requirements (including terrain), or, if none, the smallest occupied one meeting size alone. If no occupied enclosure meets size, flip none. This fallback applies to flock animals too. Playing a new release project gives 1 reputation; supporting one already in play does not.
answers.evidence: Release into the wild rules specify exact size, losses/retained gains, new-project reputation and special-enclosure-token first procedure, then smallest standard enclosure with terrain and size-only fallback.

answers.answer: Sponsors I plays exactly 1 Sponsor from hand if action strength is at least its level and its conditions are met. Sponsors II plays one or more cards if strength +1 is at least the sum of their levels; X-tokens can raise strength. Side II cards may come from hand or from within reputation range in the display, paying the folder number per card, and upgrade-required conditions are allowed. Play cards one by one, fully resolving each instant effect (except after-finishing effects) before the next. Alternatively, advance the Break token by strength and take that much money on Side I, or take twice that money on Side II. The money is the full strength amount even if the Break token has only one step left before the last space.
answers.evidence: Sponsors I/II specify hand/display options, level thresholds, folder cost, sequencing and upgraded conditions. Side I money option takes full money even if fewer steps remain; Side II money option pays twice.

answers.answer: Break order: (1) discard to hand limit, normally 3 or 5 with the particular university; (2) return Multiplier, Venom, and Constriction tokens from Action cards; (3) recall workers and replenish partner zoos/universities; (4) discard display folders 1 and 2, slide remaining cards down, and refill; (5) take income; (6) reset the Break token. Income includes appeal-track money, kiosk income, and break-income icons on Sponsors and activated map bonuses. Each kiosk earns 1 money for each adjacent unique building, special enclosure, occupied standard enclosure, or pavilion (empty standard enclosures do not qualify; empty special enclosures do). When multiple players take display cards during income, refill the display after each player. Income is usually simultaneous; if effects require ordering, start with the player who initiated the break (or the affected player closest to them), then proceed clockwise.
answers.evidence: Break procedure lists all steps and income categories, specifies kiosk qualifying neighbors and empty-enclosure exception, and gives display refill/order instructions when players take cards.

answers.answer: At 2 conservation, choose to upgrade an Action card or activate an additional worker. At 5 and 8, choose 5 money or the Bonus token next to that space (if available); the 5-money option remains when tokens are gone. The first time anyone reaches 10, all players discard one Final Scoring card; if nobody reaches 10 before game end, each player discards one before scoring. Check for the end at the end of your own turn or during a break when Appeal and Conservation are in the same scoring area or have passed one another. Gains during another player's turn wait until the end of your own turn or a break to trigger, unless someone else triggers first. The triggering player finishes their turn and everyone else takes one final turn; if triggered during a break, everyone takes one final turn. Each Final Scoring card is capped at 4 conservation points. Victory Points = Appeal minus the lowest Appeal value in the scoring area containing your Conservation counter. Highest positive total wins; tie goes to the player with most conservation-project supports, then tied players share the win.
answers.evidence: Scoring section states milestone rewards and 10-point discard rule; end timing, delayed other-player-turn gains and final turns; Final Scoring card cap; VP formula and support-count tiebreak/shared victory.
